backlogged.summary: PATH_IN_TEXT (lib/contract.mjs) only recognizes paths that contain a '/' and have an extension. A bare file name in prose, such as `t.mjs`, or a path with no extension is not detected, so a criterion can name an overlaid helper without a warning. This fits the contract's wording, so it is only a coverage note.

F82's own AC-1 sentence names test/t.mjs and test/helpers.mjs as examples while it is `new: true`, so the new rule warns about the contract that introduces it. This is harmless because the warning does not block anything, but it shows how a prose example can trigger the rule.

approve.mjs and lint-contract.mjs each read `config.verify?.test_paths` and pass it to lintContract separately. A third caller could forget to pass it, and the warning would silently turn off (the default is `[]`). A shared helper would remove that risk.
